title: Valid Palindrome II
summary: You get a string `s` of lowercase English letters. You may delete at most one character from it, or none at all. Return true if, after that, `s` reads the same forward and backward, and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Deleting the last "s" leaves "rotator". Deleting the first "r", the other half of the mismatched pair, would not work.
The first pair that differs is "l" and "m". Deleting either one still leaves a pair that differs.

constraints: s holds only lowercase English letters

approaches.twist: Skip either the left or the right character at the first mismatch, and check that the rest is a palindrome.
Delete each character in turn and check whether what's left is a palindrome.
approaches.note: Works, but n deletions with an O(n) check each take O(n²) time, about 10¹⁰ steps for 10⁵ characters. The target is O(n).

signals.phrase: reads the same forward and backward
signals.meaning: A palindrome is a row of mirrored pairs. Check them from both ends inward; only a pair that differs needs any thought.
You get one deletion. At the first pair that differs, spend it on one of those two characters. You can't tell which one, so check the rest both ways: once without each.

constraintReading: len(s) can reach 10⁵, so deleting each character in turn and checking the rest (O(n²), about 10¹⁰ steps) is far too slow. Aim for O(n): one inward pass, and after the first mismatch at most two more passes over the middle, with O(1) space.

related.relation: The same inward palindrome check with no deletion to spend, but with case and punctuation to skip.
